question: The "White Rabbit"-based IST Distribution Demonstration Network inaugurated this week at the RRSL, Jakkur (Bengaluru) is best described as:

options.text: A satellite-based navigation augmentation system replacing GAGAN
A high-precision time-distribution network delivering Indian Standard Time over optical fibre/Ethernet with sub-nanosecond accuracy
A quantum-encrypted communication link between CSIR-NPL and ISRO
A 6G spectrum-testing facility under the Ministry of Communications

explanation: The Jakkur (RRSL) network uses CERN's open-source White Rabbit technology over Ethernet/optical fibre (IEEE 1588 Precision Time Protocol) to disseminate IST with sub-nanosecond accuracy — part of the "One Nation, One Time" push led by the Legal Metrology Division with CSIR-NPL, ISRO, BSNL and SEBI.
subject: Current Affairs

question: President Droupadi Murmu's three-nation State visit this week (Moldova, North Macedonia, Romania) was notable because it marked the first-ever visit by an Indian President to:
explanation: It was the first-ever Indian presidential visit to Moldova and North Macedonia; the Romania leg was the first by an Indian President in over three decades. (Moldova and N. Macedonia are landlocked EU candidates; Romania is an EU member fronting the Black Sea.)
subject: Current Affairs

question: The Supreme Court gave conditional clearance this week to India's first (urban) night safari. It is being developed at:
explanation: The SC gave conditional clearance (subject to CEC + Central Zoo Authority + MoEFCC safeguards) to the ~Rs 1,500-crore Kukrail Reserve Forest night safari and zoo in Lucknow, UP — India's first urban night safari, confined to 855.07 ha of the reserve.
subject: Current Affairs

question: The "Semicon 2.0" programme approved by the Union Cabinet this week has a budget outlay of about:
explanation: Rs 1,27,500 crore — a big jump from the original India Semiconductor Mission's Rs 76,000 crore. Semicon 2.0 covers the full value chain (design, fab, packaging, equipment, materials, R&D, talent).
subject: Current Affairs

question: India approved its first dengue vaccine this week — QDENGA (TAK-003). Which statement is correct?

options.text: It is a single-serotype inactivated vaccine requiring pre-vaccination screening
It is a live-attenuated, tetravalent vaccine covering all four dengue serotypes and needs no pre-vaccination screening
It is an mRNA vaccine effective only against DENV-2
It is a protein-subunit vaccine approved only for those with prior dengue infection

explanation: QDENGA (TAK-003), from Takeda, is a live-attenuated tetravalent vaccine covering all four serotypes and needs no pre-vaccination screening — approved by CDSCO for ages 4–60, two doses three months apart.
subject: Current Affairs

question: The Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Bill, 2026 raises the sanctioned strength of the Supreme Court to:
explanation: The Bill raises SC strength to 38 judges. Parliament fixes the number "by law" under Article 124(1) — a simple-majority statute, not a constitutional amendment.
subject: Current Affairs

question: NITI Aayog released its first-ever Investment Friendliness Index (IFI) 2026 this week. Which State/UT topped the ranking?
explanation: Gujarat topped NITI Aayog's inaugural Investment Friendliness Index (IFI) 2026 — a cooperative/competitive-federalism tool tied to Viksit Bharat @2047.
subject: Current Affairs

question: "Vikram-1", in the news this week, is:

options.text: India's first indigenous cryogenic upper stage
A privately built Indian rocket that achieved a successful orbital launch
ISRO's new reusable launch vehicle demonstrator

explanation: Vikram-1 achieved India's first successful private orbital rocket launch (Skyroot Aerospace) — a milestone for India's private space sector.
subject: Current Affairs

question: India commissioned its first-ever geothermal wells this week at Puga Valley. Puga Valley is located in:
explanation: Ladakh. Puga Valley (a known geothermal hotspot) saw India's first-ever geothermal wells commissioned this week.
subject: Current Affairs

question: India exported the Akash surface-to-air missile system this week to two Central Asian countries, namely:
explanation: The Akash SAM was exported to Tajikistan and Turkmenistan, extending India's defence footprint into Central Asia.
subject: Current Affairs

question: The Union Cabinet approved the "Regional Connectivity Scheme – Modified UDAN" this week, with an outlay of Rs 28,840 crore over 10 years. UDAN primarily aims to:

options.text: Electrify all railway routes in hilly states
Make regional air travel affordable and revive under-served/unserved airports
Provide rural broadband via low-earth-orbit satellites
Build dedicated freight corridors for perishables

explanation: UDAN (Ude Desh ka Aam Naagrik) makes regional air travel affordable and revives under-served/unserved airports; the modified scheme adds Rs 28,840 crore over 10 years.
subject: Current Affairs

question: In the rebased Index of Core Industries (base year 2022-23) released this week, a new industry was added as the 9th core industry. It is:
explanation: Iron ore was added as the 9th core industry in the rebased Index of Core Industries (base year 2022-23).
subject: Current Affairs

question: Which of India's operational launch vehicles is primarily used to place heavy communication satellites into Geosynchronous Transfer Orbit (GTO)?
explanation: LVM3 (GSLV Mk III) — India's heaviest operational launcher — carries heavy communication satellites to GTO and human-rated for Gaganyaan. PSLV is the reliable workhorse for polar/LEO payloads.
subject: Science & Technology

question: A cryogenic rocket engine typically uses which combination of propellants?
explanation: A cryogenic engine burns liquid hydrogen (fuel) + liquid oxygen (oxidiser) at very low temperatures, giving high specific impulse.
subject: Science & Technology

question: CRISPR-Cas9, frequently in the news, is a tool for:

options.text: Precise editing of DNA sequences ("genome editing")

explanation: CRISPR-Cas9 is a genome-editing tool that makes precise cuts in DNA, enabling gene correction/insertion/deletion.
subject: Science & Technology

question: In a Pressurised Heavy Water Reactor (PHWR) — the mainstay of India's first-stage nuclear programme — the moderator and fuel are respectively:
explanation: A PHWR uses heavy water (D₂O) as moderator/coolant and natural (unenriched) uranium as fuel — India's first-stage reactor design.
subject: Science & Technology

question: The third stage of India's three-stage nuclear power programme is designed to utilise which fuel, in which the country has vast reserves?
explanation: Stage three uses thorium-232, bred into fissile uranium-233, exploiting India's large thorium (monazite) reserves. (Stage 1: PHWRs on natural U; Stage 2: fast breeder reactors using Pu-239.)
subject: Science & Technology

question: Which principle allows a quantum bit (qubit) to represent 0 and 1 simultaneously, giving quantum computers their potential advantage?
explanation: Superposition lets a qubit hold 0 and 1 states simultaneously; combined with entanglement it underpins quantum computing's parallelism.
subject: Science & Technology

question: mRNA vaccines (e.g., against COVID-19) work by:

options.text: Injecting a weakened live virus that replicates in the body
Delivering genetic instructions that prompt host cells to make a viral protein, triggering an immune response
Introducing pre-formed antibodies for immediate passive immunity
Using bacteriophages to destroy the pathogen

explanation: mRNA vaccines deliver genetic instructions so the body's own cells produce a viral antigen (e.g., the spike protein), triggering an immune response — no live virus involved.
subject: Science & Technology

question: Monoclonal antibodies are best described as:

options.text: Identical antibodies derived from a single clone of cells, engineered to target one specific antigen
A class of antiviral small molecules
Chemicals that suppress all immune activity non-specifically

explanation: Monoclonal antibodies are identical antibodies from a single cell clone, engineered to bind one specific antigen — used in therapeutics and diagnostics.
subject: Science & Technology
